mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (procuration) for the person executing the French SARL formation documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all shareholders, direct and indirect beneficial owners, gérants, authorized signatories, and external service providers against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, United Nations Security Council Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, French national asset-freezing list administered by DG Trésor, and politically exposed persons databases. Enhanced due diligence is required under Articles L561-10 and L561-10-2 of the French Monetary and Financial Code for the Medium_Risk_Enhanced maritime towage and salvage sector, including verification of source of funds, commercial counterparties, and vessel/salvage contracting history.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); official corporate-name availability verified against the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés via INPI data (https://data.inpi.fr) and the competent Greffe du tribunal de commerce.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be expressed in Latin script and must be capable of being written in French legal instruments. Under Loi Toubon, French-language versions of the articles of association, legal notice, and registration filings are mandatory. A foreign-language name may be used only with a French transliteration or a French registered trade name and a French-language statement of the corporate object. Non-Latin scripts, pictographic characters, or unverifiable transliterations are not accepted for the legal denomination.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Crédit, Caisse, Finance — banking or financing terms requiring prior authorization from ACPR or the European Central Bank
Assurance, Mutuelle, Réassurance — regulated insurance terms requiring prior ACPR licensing
Avocat, Notaire, Huissier de justice, Expert-comptable, Commissaire aux comptes — regulated professions requiring ministerial approval
France, État, République, Ministère, Commune — expressions creating a false public-entity connotation
SARL, SA, SAS, EURL — legal-form descriptors that are misleading if the entity is not duly constituted under the corresponding French corporate form
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not provide a statutory pre-incorporation name reservation; protection of a corporate name arises only upon RCS registration or separate INPI trademark filing. If the Greffe rejects the proposed name, the applicant may correct and resubmit the formation file through the Guichet unique. Where the registrar maintains an objection, the applicant may file a written challenge with the juge commis à la surveillance du registre du commerce et des sociétés within fifteen days of notification and may appeal an adverse ruling to the applicable cour d'appel within one month. A rejection based on a third-party trademark right is separately actionable before the tribunal judiciaire.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial domiciliation is acceptable solely for the registered office (siège social) of the SARL, provided it is established under a valid domiciliation contract satisfying Article L123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code and the offices are in France. For offshore towage and marine salvage operations, a virtual office is not sufficient as the sole commercial substance; the company must maintain an operational base, emergency response contact point, vessel management records, and accounting records physically accessible to the French maritime administration, customs, tax authorities, and port authorities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — estimated 70–80% likelihood of unannounced physical inspection within the first 18 months after registration, given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML/CFT classification and mandatory statutory licensing for deep-sea towage and maritime emergency salvage operations. Inspections may be performed by the French maritime administration, DGCCRF, customs (douane), or competent port and prefectoral authorities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Articles L.223-1 et seq. (SARL); Articles L.123-1 et seq. (commercial register); and Articles R.123-1 et seq. (registration formalities).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent local clerk of the Commercial Court (greffe du tribunal de commerce), through the National Institute of Industrial Property (INPI) Single Window (Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic business-creation formality submitted through the INPI Guichet unique, resulting in registration in the Registre national des entreprises and, for a commercial SARL, the Registre du commerce et des sociétés.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; capital may be set at EUR 1. At least 20% of cash contributions must be paid at incorporation, with the balance paid within five years of registration. Cash contributions are deposited with an authorized bank, notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and released after registration. Contributions in kind must be fully contributed; a commissaire aux apports is generally required unless the statutory unanimous waiver conditions are met.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accepts the subscriptions set out in its executed articles of association and acknowledges receipt of the required initial cash contributions, subject to confirmation by the depositary. RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [full address], France, and that the Manager is authorized to complete any related filing. RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed Manager (gérant) for an indefinite term, with the powers provided by law and the articles. RESOLVED, that the Manager is authorized to submit the incorporation formalities through the INPI Guichet unique, obtain registration and tax identifiers, open operating accounts, and take all lawful actions necessary to commence business, subject to obtaining required maritime, port, safety, and environmental approvals.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Approve structure and execute SARL articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders and, where relevant, a French notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Set the company name, registered office, corporate purpose, capital, ownership, management, and financial year. Execute the articles of association; use notarization only where legally required, including relevant transfers of real estate or other notarial acts. Arrange certified French translations of foreign-language evidence where requested.
required_dossiers: Manager identity, address, and acceptance of office
Statement of beneficial owners and ownership chain
Valuation report for in-kind contributions, or documentation supporting a lawful waiver
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistencies between the articles, identity evidence, ownership disclosures, and proposed corporate purpose; obtain missing signatures, translations, or valuation evidence before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit cash capital and obtain deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked formation-capital account, provide the executed articles and subscriber details, and deposit at least 20% of subscribed cash capital. Obtain the certificate of deposit for the registration dossier. Request release of the funds after the company is registered.
required_dossiers: Draft or executed articles of association
Proof of identity and address for depositors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve bank compliance queries with source-of-funds and ownership-chain evidence; if a bank declines onboarding, approach another authorized depositary or a notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal-announcement journal (journal d'annonces légales) for the registered-office département
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the prescribed formation notice after execution of the articles and retain the publication certificate. Ensure the notice accurately states the corporate name, legal form, capital, registered office, purpose, duration, and manager details.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrected notice and replacement certificate if any mandatory particulars are missing or inconsistent with the articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the creation formality and beneficial-owner filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI National Single Window (Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises); registration processed by the competent Commercial Court clerk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic creation formality, attach the required evidence, declare beneficial owners, pay applicable registry charges, and respond through the portal to requests for information. The filing generates the RNE and RCS registration process; retain the registration extract and SIREN/SIRET identifiers.
required_dossiers: Manager's identity, address, and non-conviction declaration where required
Required foreign-entity documents, legalization or apostille, and French translations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer portal or registry queries within the stated deadline, amend the electronic filing, and upload corrected or additional evidence. Escalate a prolonged or disputed registration issue to the competent registry clerk or applicable formalities support channel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration corporate and tax records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Manager; French tax administration (Direction générale des Finances publiques); relevant social-security bodies if employing staff
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Release deposited capital, open the operating bank account, maintain the statutory register of decisions and accounting records, and verify VAT and corporate-tax registration details. Register as an employer before hiring and complete required employment declarations.
required_dossiers: Employment and social-security registration documents, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax or social-registration data with the responsible administration and preserve filing acknowledgments; do not commence regulated operations solely on the basis of company registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No general industrial licensing board applies to offshore towage and salvage. The competent maritime authorities include the Directorate General for Maritime Affairs, Fisheries and Aquaculture (DGAMPA), the relevant regional maritime authority and departmental directorate for territories and the sea (DDTM), and the competent maritime prefect and port authority, according to vessel, port, and operating location.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No single nationwide offshore towage or salvage operating licence applies in all cases. Required approvals depend on the operation and may include French vessel registration and authorization to sail, vessel safety and manning certificates, port access or occupation authorization, and case-specific maritime, environmental, or salvage permissions. Confirm requirements with DGAMPA, the competent DDTM, maritime prefect, and port authority before contracting or mobilizing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition, Biodiversity, and Climate and Nature Negotiations; competent environmental authority determined under the French Environmental Code.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Conditional, not automatically exempt. Apply the Environmental Code project-screening rules, including Article R.122-2 and its annex, for any qualifying project, vessel-related infrastructure, dredging, seabed works, or port development. The competent authority determines case-by-case screening or requires an environmental impact assessment where thresholds or likely significant effects apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with applicable French and EU rules governing vessel discharges, oil and hazardous-substance releases, sewage, garbage, air emissions, and port reception facilities, including MARPOL as implemented in France. Obtain any required water-law authorization for discharges or works; comply with site-specific permit limits and waste traceability requirements. No universal wastewater or VOC numeric threshold can be assigned without the vessel, installation, discharge, and location.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before operations, obtain applicable vessel safety, seaworthiness, crew qualification, and manning documentation; secure port or site access and any required fire-safety approval for shore facilities. Shore premises must meet applicable building, fire, and workplace requirements, including employer risk assessment and occupational-safety duties. Structural-load inspection or facility-specific civil-defence clearance is required where applicable to the premises or project, not as a universal SARL incorporation condition.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), administered through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) or, for non-established businesses, the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE). Principal digital portal: impots.gouv.fr. Corporate formation and business registration are filed through the Guichet unique operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI). Customs registration and EORI administration are handled by the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects (DGDDI) through douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate or register the SARL through the INPI Guichet unique and obtain its national SIREN identifier and establishment-level SIRET identifier. 2. File the initial business tax registration information with the competent SIE through the applicable French tax-registration process. 3. Apply for a French VAT identification number consisting of the prefix FR followed by a two-digit control key and the nine-digit SIREN number. The number is issued by the DGFiP after verification of the entity, activity, management, premises, and expected taxable transactions. 4. A non-established foreign entity carrying out French taxable transactions must apply to the SIEE unless another French establishment or fiscal representative arrangement is legally applicable. 5. Obtain an EORI number from French customs before importing or exporting goods in the European Union customs territory. 6. Maintain constitutional documents, registry extract, beneficial-owner information, bank details, contracts, invoices, customs records, and evidence of economic activity. VAT registration may be required even where the domestic small-business franchise threshold is not exceeded, including where the business makes intra-Community acquisitions, imports, exports, or transactions for which reverse-charge rules apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS), currently at a standard rate of 25% subject to applicable conditions and reliefs. Certain SARLs may elect temporary income-tax treatment under the statutory partnership-style regime, generally for up to five fiscal years and subject to legal eligibility conditions, including qualifying ownership, size, age, and activity requirements. A qualifying family SARL may elect income-tax treatment without the ordinary five-year limitation, subject to the family-ownership and activity conditions. France has no United States-style general check-the-box election. Entity classification is determined by French company law and tax statutes. Anti-hybrid mismatch rules implement the relevant EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive provisions and can deny deductions, include income, or otherwise neutralize mismatches; they are not elective classification mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT), governed principally by the French General Tax Code and the EU VAT Directive. French VAT applies according to the place-of-supply rules, including special rules for maritime transport, towing, salvage, services connected with vessels, imports, intra-Community transactions, and business-to-business services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The principal French domestic franchise-in-base threshold for services is EUR 37,500 of prior-year turnover, with a higher tolerance threshold of EUR 41,250 subject to statutory conditions. For activities principally involving supplies of goods, the ordinary thresholds are EUR 85,000 and EUR 93,500 respectively. These thresholds concern eligibility for the small-business VAT exemption and do not eliminate VAT registration obligations arising from imports, intra-Community transactions, reverse-charge transactions, taxable French establishments, or special sector rules. Offshore towing and salvage revenues must be analyzed transaction-by-transaction because the place of supply and maritime exemptions may apply independently of turnover thresholds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not currently operate a universal real-time VAT invoice-clearance system for all domestic transactions. The enacted electronic-invoicing reform requires all businesses established in France to be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026. Issuance obligations are phased: large enterprises and in-scope intermediate-sized enterprises from 1 September 2026, and small and medium-sized enterprises and micro-enterprises from 1 September 2027, subject to legislative implementation details and permitted extensions. Electronic invoices must generally use a compliant structured or hybrid format and be transmitted through an approved private platform (plateforme de dématérialisation partenaire, PDP), with the public directory supporting routing. Electronic reporting of relevant transaction and payment data, including certain cross-border transactions and transactions with non-business customers, will apply on the applicable reform timetable. Current VAT invoices must contain mandatory particulars, permit reliable identification of the issuer and recipient, preserve integrity and authenticity, and be retained for the statutory period. No general digital stamp or pre-issuance DGFiP clearance is presently required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to a destination outside the European Union may be invoiced without French VAT where the goods are dispatched or transported outside the EU by the seller or by the customer, and the exporter can substantiate the export through customs evidence and matching commercial records. Intra-Community supplies of goods may qualify for exemption rather than domestic zero-rating where the statutory customer VAT-identification, transport, and reporting conditions are satisfied. Services supplied to a business established outside France are generally outside the scope of French VAT under the B2B general place-of-supply rule, rather than technically zero-rated; the customer’s status and location must be documented. Services connected with vessels, towing, salvage, freight, and emergency maritime operations require separate analysis under the specific place-of-supply and exemption provisions. Relevant exemptions may apply to qualifying sea-going vessels, their equipment, and specified services, but they are conditional and do not automatically cover every offshore contract. A French VAT refund or deduction claim requires valid purchase invoices, direct business use, correct VAT treatment, accounting records, and proof that any export or exempt activity satisfies the applicable legal conditions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration and MRN, with customs exit confirmation or equivalent electronic evidence of exit from the European Union
Commercial invoice, contract, purchase order, and detailed description of the goods or maritime equipment
Packing list and transport documentation, including bill of lading, sea waybill, or equivalent carrier evidence where applicable
Evidence identifying the exporter, consignee, destination outside the European Union, and transport chain
Evidence of delivery or receipt outside the European Union where required to corroborate the export file
Applicable export authorisations, licences, sanctions-screening records, and vessel or cargo documentation
VAT records linking the export declaration, invoice, accounting entry, customs MRN, and transport evidence
Bank payment evidence or other commercial settlement evidence; France does not generally require a standalone inward-remittance certificate as a statutory condition for export VAT exemption
For intra-Community supplies, the customer’s valid EU VAT number, transport evidence, and required EC Sales List reporting records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.mandatory_fx_repatriation_deadline_days: No general French statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline applies to export proceeds, and 180 days is not a generally applicable French rule. France has no general exchange-control requirement requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days. Banks may impose contractual or anti-money-laundering documentation requirements, and sector-specific, financing, sanctions, customs, or subsidy rules may impose separate conditions.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP may deny or reverse the VAT exemption or deduction and assess the unpaid VAT, late-payment interest, and applicable penalties where export, transport, customer status, vessel qualification, or place-of-supply evidence is incomplete or false. The standard tax penalty may be 40% for deliberate failure and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights; a 5% penalty may apply in specified invoicing or reporting situations, while a 10% penalty can apply to certain late-payment or filing defaults. Late-payment interest is generally charged at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. False or fabricated customs or tax documents may trigger customs penalties, criminal tax-fraud exposure, sanctions-related consequences, and recovery from the relevant transaction date. Ineligible input-VAT refunds may be clawed back with interest and penalties. The administration can conduct documentary or on-site audits, require production of customs and transport records, compare VAT returns with customs data, examine bank and accounting evidence, and apply joint-and-several liability or intermediary liability where legally available.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) and Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) for balance-of-payments reporting; Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) for banking supervision
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a full Eurozone member with complete current account and capital account convertibility under EU law. Profit remittance is unrestricted for EU parent entities; for non-EU shareholders, France applies no quantitative FX controls but imposes mandatory balance-of-payments (BOP) reporting to the Banque de France for cross-border flows exceeding EUR 750,000 per calendar month or for all direct investment transactions. Dividends to non-resident companies are subject to withholding tax unless reduced by tax treaty (commonly 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive with minimum holding requirements; otherwise 25% / treaty-reduced). No material hurdles to profit repatriation exist beyond standard corporate tax, dividend withholding tax, and anti-abuse compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose any statutory timeline for surrender of export proceeds or mandatory conversion ratios. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency or converted freely. However, all cross-border direct investment transactions and any transaction exceeding EUR 750,000 require submission of BOP declarations to the Banque de France via the FIBI reporting system. For marine salvage services rendered to non-residents, proceeds must be booked as services exports and reported under BOP heading 'Services - Transportation / Other services' as applicable; no FX conversion is mandated.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR multicurrency) and Capital Escrow Account (dedicated blocked account for contractual escrow)
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Treasury / Hedging Line
Operational Account (limited for complex cross-border trade finance)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with significant legal constraints. French-regulated EMIs (licensed under ACPR with e-money passport) such as Qonto, Shine, or Lydia/SumUp may open accounts remotely and facilitate EUR clearing, but they generally do not provide SWIFT correspondent banking, letters of credit, or escrow-grade maritime salvage services. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Lithuania-licensed, UK-licensed, or non-EEA) face restricted viability: French AML/KYC rules (Code Monétaire et Financier, Art. L561 et seq.) treat such providers as higher-risk non-bank counterparties; French banks frequently reject transfers from unregulated or offshore EMIs; and commercial counterparties in salvage/towage (Lloyd's market, insurers, shipowners) typically require settlement through a licensed EU bank. Rating: Medium for local ACPR-licensed EMI as operational sub-account; Low for offshore EMI as primary clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not legally mandated for opening a corporate bank account in France, but ACPR compliance practice and most tier-1 banks require at least one director or the statutory representative (gérant) to attend an in-person or live video-identity verification appointment. Pure remote account opening is available only through licensed Fintechs or with enhanced video-KYC using certified identity verification; however, for the maritime salvage industry (classified as 'Medium-Risk Enhanced'), the bank's RCCI (Compliance) committee will typically demand in-person interview for ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) holding 25% or more, unless the entity has an existing banking relationship or the UBO is a recognised EU listed company. Statutory mandate: Physical presence is not impossible, but practical bank policy makes it near-mandatory for first-time SARL account opening of a medium-risk entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Salvage/towage payments from offshore maritime jurisdictions (e.g., Marshall Islands, Panama, Liberia) or from P&I Clubs / underwriters with opaque payment chains
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete salvage service contract (LSF 2000 / Lloyd's Open Form or BIMCO towcon), voyage orders, crew manifests, vessel registry extracts, invoice matching each disbursement, and an operational narrative confirming the service vessel and rescue event. Provide UBO structure chart, corporate register extract, bank reference from existing relationship bank, and proof of registration under ISIC 5222 / French Équipement Sécurité Maritime with relevant statutory licence (if applicable).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid inbound capital injection exceeding EUR 750,000 without economic justification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital contribution resolution from SARL shareholders (gérant minutes), notarised share subscription or share premium deed, bank statement of the transferring entity, share register (registre des mouvements de titres), and confirmation in writing that transfer qualifies as a direct investment under France's BOP rules (Book IV of Monetary and Financial Code). Provide source of wealth documentation for the investor and any tax clearance from the foreign tax authority, as requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disbursements to sanctioned or high-risk flags, ship chandlers, or subcontractors in non-OECD jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-voyage due diligence package including Sanctions and PEP screening of all payees (OFAC, EU, UN, HMT), export-controlled service license check (no dual-use technology), proof of vessel flag conformity, crew nationality list, and contractual warranties that the tug/salvage operation did not service sanctioned entities. Maintain transactional audit trail and real-time screening report from a recognised compliance provider (e.g., Dow Jones, World-Check, Dun & Bradstreet).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Earmarking for 'Lloyds Standard Form Wire' without supporting insurance/salvage documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the salvage arbitration or open-form agreement, Lloyds Form notification and counter-signature, salvage master's report (CASEM / CASR), interim assessment of the security fund, and an escrow instruction letter from Lloyd's salvage arbitration branch or appointed sole broker. Include all correspondence evidencing the award calculation or interim security.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for shareholder capital injection: 1) Use SWIFT MT103 wire from investor's bank to the SARL's EUR account in France (BNP Paribas, Société Générale, or Crédit Agricole). 2) Purpose code must state 'Direct Investment in Capital' — under French reporting use BOP form 'Déclaration de transaction (FIBI)' with тип 'CAPITAL / DIVIDEND / TRANSFER'. Use the official French purpose code '51' for investments / contributions to capital, or mention 'capital increase / numéraire' in free text field. 3) For transfers exceeding EUR 750,000 per month, the bank will require the BOP reporting declaration to be completed by the account holder within 20 days following the end of the month in which the transfer occurred; otherwise the bank may block the wire. 4) Verify the resident investor identity and UBO beneficial owner; a French SARL with non-resident UBO must produce the 'Gérant' identity, corporate registry Kbis, and a certified copy of the shareholder resolution. 5) For escrow structures involving Lloyd's salvage security, funds should be tagged in the account reference as 'ESCROW - Salvage Security' and a separate escrow sub-account opened at the same banking institution to avoid commingling.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Preferred clearing rail for outbound service/disbursement: (a) Standard commercial trade settlements for maritime services are executed via SWIFT MT103/2 and target2/SEPA in EUR; for non-EUR settlement use SWIFT MT103 with USD/GBP nostro accounts. For salvage-casualty disbursements, require payment in accordance with Lloyd's Standard Form terms (if contractually specified): payment to the salvor's nominated Euro account via MT103 with purpose code 'Settlement of salvage remuneration' (Services - Other business services). (b) For contracts involving the physical repair of tugboats or equipment procurement, a Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) is recommended under UCP600 with bill-of-lading or delivery certificate as documents; given service nature, standby LCs (ISBP745) for security guarantees also apply. (c) For subcontracting disbursements (fuel, ship chandlery, crew wages), use direct MT103 with references to the contract line item and pre-cleared beneficiary banking compliance. (d) Any USD or GBP invoice from Lloyd's arbitrators or P&I Club is to be settled via USD/GBP conversion at the bank's commercial FX rate with execution on same-day value for spot conversions, or via forward contracts to manage settlement risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD spot and outright forwards for operational settlement
EUR/GBP spot and outright forwards for Lloyds / P&I Club settlements
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) is available in limited EUR/USD cases but not standard for Eurozone entities; the primary route is deliverable forwards with ACPR-licensed counterparty
Cross-currency swap (CCS) for converting injected capital into EUR if shareholder's base currency is USD or GBP
FX options (European style) for the purpose of hedging salvage awards denominated in foreign currencies, subject to bank's ISDA/CSA contractual documentation
Currency swap with maturity matching to the salvage arbitration timeline

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts by the shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the SARL; minutes retained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure may result in a court injunction, civil liability of the manager, and fines; no automatic statutory strike-off deadline applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of approved annual accounts and required management documents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the French business formalities portal operated by INPI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or within two months after approval when filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or missing filing may result in a fine of approximately EUR 1,500, increased to approximately EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance, a court injunction, and potential registry enforcement; no fixed automatic strike-off period applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and financial schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally electronically by the second business day after 1 May for a calendar-year company; otherwise within three months after the financial year-end, subject to the applicable filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a 10% surcharge, statutory interest, estimated assessment, and additional penalties for material or intentional non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual value-added tax return, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual CA12 return generally due within three months after the financial year-end for the simplified VAT regime; monthly or quarterly VAT returns apply under the normal regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate filing may trigger a 10% surcharge, statutory interest, estimated assessment, and VAT penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due electronically by the second business day after 1 May when the company is within the applicable CVAE filing scope
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure or delay may trigger tax surcharges, statutory interest, estimated assessment, and administrative penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French business formalities portal and National Register of Enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven; generally within 30 days after becoming aware of a change in beneficial ownership or control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain accurate information may result in criminal penalties, injunctions, and restrictions affecting the company's registration status; there is no annual confirmation filing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally required when the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional group-company rules may apply.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French generally accepted accounting principles under the Autorité des normes comptables; IFRS is generally not mandatory for an individual SARL and may apply principally in qualifying consolidated-accounting contexts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France has no general annual UBO confirmation filing and no annual confirmation solely for shareholding transfers. The SARL must maintain accurate beneficial ownership information and file an update generally within 30 days after a reportable change. Share transfers must be documented and recorded in the company's corporate records and, where required, declared to the tax administration and registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register or file of shareholder decisions and meeting minutes
Register of share transfers and supporting transfer instruments
Current register or record of shareholders and capital ownership
Corporate records evidencing appointment and removal of managers
Beneficial ownership records and filed declarations

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately 650-1,950 per year, depending on location and included administrative services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately 3,000-12,000 per year when a statutory auditor is required; otherwise 0

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% on first €42,500 taxable profit for SMEs (turnover ≤ €50M), 25% thereafter; R&D tax credit up to 30% of qualifying expenses

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1201 - Déclaration de résultat via impots.gouv.fr electronic platform
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after fiscal year-end (e.g. 31 March for calendar year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Consolidate group revenues if non-resident parent involved

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Incorporate transfer pricing adjustments and economic substance compliance

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 0.5% of tax due per month of delay, minimum €50, maximum 25% of tax due; criminal prosecution for evasion

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TRC (Demande de réduction de précompte) with supporting documents to French tax authorities for DTA relief; processing within 2 months
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% under most double tax treaties; Interest: 0% within EU, 10% otherwise

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million consolidated revenue for local file; €750 million for master file
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: French Economic Substance Regulations apply to certain entities; maritime salvage operations generally require adequate substance to avoid recharacterization

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income or false declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Up to 5 years imprisonment and fines up to 80% of evaded tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for restitution, disqualification, fines, and possible imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creation of artificial entities without genuine economic activity for tax avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1.5 million or 80% of annual turnover; criminal penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, disqualification from office, and imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform KYC/CDD or report suspicious transactions in cross-border dealings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million or 5% of turnover; imprisonment up to 1 year
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability including fines and potential jail time for responsible executives
